How do you get into that gig? I'm a fast/accurate typer... what kind of skills are required?

Well, it's not going to be easy. And it's worth noting, live captions and offline timing are TOTALLY different jobs.

Live is done with a stenotype machine, not a normal keyboard, and it's a very high pressure job. If you have stenographer training or experience try submitting your resume to some local broadcasters in your area.

Now offline CC timing is just one of the many services offered at the studio I work with. It's not something that really needs fast typing skills; you're dealing with lots of text parsing from scripts, and transcripts (usually all terribly inaccurate) and breaking them down into 26 or 32 char breakpoints. Then ingesting those into captioning software to then play and time the captions in time with video playback.

It sounds easy, but it's very tedious, irritating at times when the content sucks, and takes way more time than you think to complete.

As for how I got into it, it was a fluke on my part, I managed to score the gig working with this guy who was solo for 26 years. He's a wealth of experience and I'm pretty much capable of any major post activity.
